messages:
maria: Quick sync — planning a k6 soak next Wed (Apr 17) to replay prod traces and validate batching / KV cache hit behavior. Dataset: s3://prod-replays/2026-04-10-replay.tar.gz (sharded). Target avg ~1.8k RPS, peak ~3k. Run 4h with 30m warmup. Regression trigger = p95 latency +20% OR error rate >0.5%. Who can own runbook/smoke checks, flamegraphs, and rollback policy?

jordan: I can own the runbook + smoke checks. Will add preflight scripts to infra repo and wire a simple healthcheck that hits /v1/health and a small chatty prompt to validate model routing.

alex: I'll take profiling/flamegraphs. Plan: capture eBPF perf and JFR (where available) at 30m intervals. I'll upload artifacts to s3://perf-uploads/soak/apr17/. Need the k6 env + a flag to enable debug traces on a subset (5% of traffic).

sarah: Important: make sure replay uses production routing policy (smart routing) so we exercise fallback paths. If we pin a model, we won't catch fallback regressions. Also please lock the model version mapping used in prod for reproducibility.

tim: For rollback policy — recommend: on >1% 5xx OR p95 +30% auto-scale-down and revert to `redwood-v1-small` model variant. Ops should be able to flip the toggle in console quickly. Who can add that toggle+runbook step?

mike: Quick Q: are we using k6 or Locust for this? k6 is fine for HTTP replays and controlling RPS. If we need complex session state, we might use Locust, but sounds like k6 fits.

qa: I'll own the scenario validation and post-run checks. I'll add automated assertions for SLOs and a script to snapshot token breakdown per route. Can we include a synthetic user flow that exercises inference with long prefix tokens?

ajenkins-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled replay job created for 2026-04-17 02:00 UTC -> 06:00 UTC. Link: https://console/redwood/runs/soak-apr17 (auto-notify ops). :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Reserved dedicated capacity window 2026-04-17 01:30-06:30 UTC on cluster `dedicated-soak-3`. Autoscaling paused during window, burst buffer = 20% extra. Please ack so we don't accidentally use it elsewhere.

alex: k6 config snippet I'll use (will commit to infra repo under tests/k6/soak-apr17.js):

```js
export let options = {
  stages: [ { duration: '30m', target: 1800 }, { duration: '3h', target: 1800 }, { duration: '30m', target: 0 } ],
  rps: 3000, // cap peak
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration{p50}': ['p(95)<500'], 'http_req_failed': ['rate<0.005'] },
}
```

Command to start (local/CI): `scripts/replay_run.sh --source s3://prod-replays/2026-04-10-replay.tar.gz --duration 4h --rps 1800 --tags soak,apr17`

jordan: I'll add a preflight step to run a tiny dry-run at 10% scale and a smoke smoke-check that validates model selection and KV cache hit ratio > 60% during warmup.

maria: great — owners: runbook/smoke=jordan, profiling/alex, QA=qa, rollback=tim. @infra-bot please keep the dedicated reservation. I'll draft the runbook and link here tomorrow. If anyone sees major gaps call it out now. :eyes:

tim: Noted. I'll also add a quick rollback playbook (commands + console toggle) and a slack alert channel `#soak-alerts` for automated SLO trips.

mike: one last ask — can we tag the replay with `replay-id=apr17-v1` so post-run tooling can correlate with traces and flamegraphs?

alex: done — will add `replay-id` tag to k6 env and artifact uploads.

maria: thanks all. I'll follow up with the draft runbook and a short checklist (preflight, dry-run, main run, capture artifacts, post-run checks, rollback). Meeting only if blockers pop up. :rocket:
